q: What computer-based system centrally monitors and controls building systems?
n: A building management system (BMS) is a computer-based control system that centrally monitors and controls HVAC, lighting, power, fire and security systems. Source: ASHRAE Guideline 13 (control systems); BMS manufacturer literature.

q: What visual or audible device warns occupants of fire?
n: A fire alarm (bell, horn, strobe) is the notification device that warns occupants. Detectors only sense smoke or heat. Source: NFPA 72, National Fire Alarm Code; RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: Which local company primarily sells building systems such as security and communication products?
n: Dexterton Corporation is a Philippine company supplying security, fire and communication systems for buildings. Source: Dexterton company website.

q: What self-contained system of cameras, recorders and monitors is used for surveillance?
n: Closed-circuit television (CCTV) is a self-contained system of cameras, recorders and monitors whose signal is not openly broadcast, used for surveillance. Source: IEC 62676 (video surveillance systems).

q: Which intercom station controls the whole system?
n: The master station is the intercom unit that can call, monitor and control all the substations in the system. Source: Intercom manufacturer literature (Aiphone, Commax).

q: For an office layout with supervisors and multiple workstations, which communication system is most appropriate?
n: A PABX gives each supervisor and workstation an internal extension, internal calling and shared outside lines, the right system for a multi-desk office. Source: Telecommunications design references; ANSI/TIA-568.

q: Why shouldn't telephone and power wires share a run?
n: Power wiring induces electrical noise (interference) in nearby telephone and data lines, so the two are run in separate conduits or with separation. Source: ANSI/TIA-569 (pathways and spaces); Philippine Electrical Code.

q: Moving to a bigger office with heavy cabling, what else besides floor area must be checked?
n: Heavy cabling needs room for raised floors or overhead cable trays, so the floor-to-ceiling height must be checked as well as the floor area. Source: ANSI/TIA-569; BICSI Telecommunications Distribution Methods Manual.

q: What is the best location for telephone lines?
o: At the center of the road
Under the sidewalk on narrow roads and under the road on wider roads
n: Telephone lines are commonly placed near the curb in the utility strip, where they are easy to reach for maintenance and stay away from the roadway. Source: DPWH and utility planning guidelines; DICT/utility standards.

q: What is an important consideration in the design layout of an IT company?
n: IT companies change teams and layouts often and carry heavy cabling, so modular furniture that is reconfigurable and has cable management is an important design consideration. Source: Time-Saver Standards for Building Types (offices); BIFMA guidelines.

q: What is the standard color for communication line piping?
n: Communication (telecom) conduits are commonly color-coded orange to distinguish them from power and other services. Source: Utility color codes (APWA uniform color code: orange for communications).

q: What is the primary challenge when installing a PABX system in an existing room?
n: In an existing finished room, the hard part of installing a PABX is running the new wiring through walls and ceilings to every extension. Source: BICSI Telecommunications Distribution Methods Manual.

q: What is the main advantage of a PABX in an office?
n: A PABX routes calls efficiently between internal extensions and shares outside lines, so staff can call each other without using external lines. Source: Telecommunications design references.

q: What network connects computers within one office building?
n: A LAN (local area network) connects computers within one office or building. A WAN connects distant sites and a MAN covers a city. Source: IEEE 802 standards overview.

q: What is the main function of an intercom?
n: An intercom provides internal two-way voice communication between rooms or stations within a building. Source: Intercom manufacturer literature.

q: Which device is used to amplify a Wi-Fi signal from the main server?
n: A router (with access points) distributes and extends the Wi-Fi signal from the main line through the space. Source: Networking equipment literature; IEEE 802.11.

q: Which is used for surveillance?
n: CCTV is the surveillance system: cameras with recording and monitoring. Source: IEC 62676 (video surveillance systems).

q: In a BPO office, which system best hides network and power cables neatly and safely?
n: A raised access floor routes network and power cables underneath to each workstation neatly and safely, and can be reconfigured. It is common in BPO offices and data rooms. Source: CISCA raised access floor guidelines; ANSI/TIA-569.

q: In a BPO office that shares data across departments, which system makes sharing efficient?
n: A LAN links all workstations and servers so data is shared across departments. Source: IEEE 802 standards overview.

q: For private room-to-room talk in a BPO office, which system fits?
n: An intercom is meant for private internal voice communication between rooms. Source: Intercom manufacturer literature.

q: PABX stands for:
n: PABX = Private Automatic Branch Exchange, a private telephone switching system serving an organization's extensions. Source: ITU telecommunications terminology.

q: ISDN stands for:
n: ISDN = Integrated Services Digital Network, a digital telephone network carrying voice and data together. Source: ITU-T I-series recommendations.

q: BMS stands for:
n: BMS = Building Management System. A BMS centrally monitors and controls HVAC, lighting, security and other building systems to save energy and keep conditions comfortable. Source: ASHRAE Guideline 13; BMS manufacturer literature.

q: FACP stands for:
n: FACP = Fire Alarm Control Panel, the unit that receives detector signals and activates alarms and other fire safety functions. Source: NFPA 72.

q: FDAS stands for:
n: FDAS = Fire Detection and Alarm System, required for many occupancies under the Fire Code. Source: RA 9514 Fire Code RIRR 2019.

q: Which of the following is a well-known brand of intercom systems?
n: Aiphone is a Japanese company specializing in intercom and entry security systems. Source: Aiphone company website.

q: Which is a leading maker of routers and network switches?
n: Cisco Systems is a leading maker of routers and network switches. Cisco's routers and switches form the backbone of most enterprise and building data networks, alongside makers such as Juniper and HPE Aruba. Source: Cisco company website.

q: Which brand is known for telephone systems and cordless phones?
n: Panasonic is well known for business telephone systems (PABX) and cordless phones. Source: Panasonic company website.

q: Which brand is best known for structured cabling?
n: Panduit is known for structured cabling and connectivity infrastructure. Source: Panduit company website.

q: Which brand specializes in consumer routers, modems and mesh Wi-Fi?
n: TP-Link specializes in consumer routers, modems and mesh Wi-Fi systems. Source: TP-Link company website.

q: In an office, which system handles room-to-room communication?
n: Room-to-room communication in an office is handled by an intercom system. Source: Intercom manufacturer literature.

q: What system is typically used for room-to-desk communication?
n: Direct room-to-desk voice communication uses an intercom (master and substations), not internet, CATV or CCTV. Source: Intercom manufacturer literature.

q: Which system handles internal calls between departments in a large office?
n: A PABX switches internal calls between department extensions and shares outside trunk lines. Source: Telecommunications design references; ANSI/TIA-568.

q: Which system is used for announcements in schools, malls and public buildings?
n: A paging or public address (PA) system broadcasts announcements and music to zones of a school, mall or public building. Source: IEC 60268 (sound system equipment); NFPA 72 (emergency voice communication).

q: Which system allows voice and video at building entrances?
n: A video intercom (video door phone) lets occupants see and talk to visitors at the entrance before letting them in. Source: Intercom manufacturer literature (Aiphone, Commax).
